title: BA1/331/2023 of RITIK ALIAS RITIK Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No. 331 of 2023
Ritik @ Ritik Vishwakarma .... Applicant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ..... Respondent
Mr. Harshit Sanwal, Advocate for the applicant.
Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, A.G.A. along with Mrs. Shiwali Joshi, Brief
Holder for the State of Uttarakhand.
Dated : 12.06.2023
Hon'ble Vivek Bharti Sharma, J. (Oral)
 Applicant Ritik @ Ritik Vishwakarma, who is
in judicial custody in F.I.R./Case Crime No.82 of 2022
(Special Sessions Trial No. 02 of 2023), under Sections
342 and 376 of I.P.C. and Section 3/4 of the Protection
of Children from Sexual Offences Act, Police Station
Kotwali Uttarkashi, District Uttarkashi, has sought his
release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the material available on file.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that the age of the applicant/accused is only 16
years at the time of incident and in the statements
recorded before the Magistrate under Section 164 of
Cr.P.C., the prosecutrix/victim did not say anything
against the applicant/accused; that, the prosecutrix only
stated that the applicant/accused and the victim were
friends and she has gone to his room of her own will &

2
volition and ate food. The victim has also stated that the
applicant/accused and the co-accused suggested that it
was already late at night, therefore, she stayed overnight
and nothing did happen with the victim during that
night. Learned counsel for the applicant/accused takes
the Court to the statements recorded in the lower court
(Annexed at Page No. 99 with the supplementary
affidavit) that the applicant/accused is an innocent
person; that, he has falsely been implicated in the
instant crime; that, he is in judicial custody since
09.10.2022 and the trial is likely to take some time and
no purpose would be served by keeping the
applicant/accused in jail.
4. Ms. Manisha Rana Singh, A.G.A for the State
vehemently opposed the bail application, however, she
admits that in her statements recorded under Section
164 of Cr.P.C., she did not state that she was sexually
assaulted by the applicant/accused.
5. Perusal of the statement of the victim shows
that the prosecutrix clearly stated that no physical
relationship was made by the applicant/accused only he
had kissed her.

3
6. In view of the above, but, without expressing
any opinion on the merits of the case before the trial
court, this Court is of the view that this is a case fit for
bail.
7. The bail application is, accordingly, allowed.
8. Let the applicant be released on bail on
furnishing bail bond with two sureties in the amount of
Rs. 40,000/- and personal bond in the like amount to
the satisfaction of the Court concerned.
 (Vivek Bharti Sharma, J.)
 12.06.2023
Akash
